member.name: T:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.UI.Input.Pointer
member.summary: An on-screen mouse cursor for pointer-driven UIs (e.g. an HDMI monitor with a USB mouse, where there is no touch panel). It draws an arrow on top of the whole UI and turns pointer motion + the left button into the framework's normal touch events, so every existing control works unchanged.
member.remarks:
The device-specific part (reading a USB-host mouse, a trackball, etc.) stays in the application; it just feeds this class:
var pointer = new Pointer(Application.Current); // when the mouse reports movement / a button: pointer.MoveTo(x, y); // or pointer.MoveBy(dx, dy) pointer.SetLeftButton(pressed); // press = touch-down, release = touch-up, move-while-pressed = drag pointer.Visible = false; // e.g. when the mouse is unplugged
The cursor is drawn via and only invalidates its own small rectangle as it moves, so it costs almost nothing to render and never triggers a full-screen repaint. All members are safe to call from any thread (the mouse driver's worker thread included); they marshal onto the UI dispatcher internally.
